title: Paydown Needed to Meet the Rural Home Loans Escrow Waiver Loan-to-Value Limit
content:
**Clause.** The escrow waiver loan-to-value limit of a Rural Home Loans loan is the product's escrow waiver maximum loan-to-value of the home's original value, tested on the principal balance on the loan record. The paydown is the principal balance less the limit amount, rounded to the cent, and nothing when the balance is already at or below it.

## The paydown as a definition

1. **Limit amount:** the home's original value on the loan record multiplied by the product's escrow waiver maximum loan-to-value and divided by 100, rounded to the cent.
2. **Balance tested:** the principal balance on the loan record.
3. **Paydown:** the balance tested less the limit amount, rounded to the cent; nothing when that is zero or less.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs, a limit of 80 percent)

| Original value | Limit amount | Principal balance | Paydown |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300000.00 | 240000.00 | 251234.56 | 11234.56 |
| 300000.00 | 240000.00 | 240000.00 | nothing (at the limit) |
| 300000.00 | 240000.00 | 239000.00 | nothing (below the limit) |
| 187654.32 | 150123.46 | 152000.00 | 1876.54 |

## Basis Q&A

**Which value is the limit applied to?** The home's original value on the loan record.

**Is a balance exactly at the limit amount within it?** Yes; the paydown is then nothing.
